1484868543426576384 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 21 🔁 2
I tend to think about imaginal practice in two basic categories: 

1) Respectable Practice

2) What-The-Fuck Practice
↓
1484869051541295109 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 14
Respectable Practice is almost everything I see:

If someone walks in on you doing imaginal practice, and what they see is someone sitting and breathing with their eyes closed, that’s respectable.
↓
1484869249143226370 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 19 🔁 1
WTF practices are the ones where if anyone sees you doing them, they will have no fucking clue what you’re doing and will probably think differently of you afterward.
↓
1484870057679327250 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 31
I taught one of my favorite practices last month, I call it The Mead Hall. 

The short version is that you let your body, voice, and breath find a rhythm, and you up the intensity again and again until it takes you over.
↓
1484870059264778253 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 26
If you see me doing this in full swing, it will basically look like me jumping and swaying and shouting a mix of rough sounds, rhyming couplets, and rhythmic notes in different registers.
↓
1484870522076897288 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 22
The WTF practices tend to be much less common,,,

But hot damn if they don’t light folks on fire from the inside out when one clicks ❤️‍🔥
↓
1484870724162621448 [2022-01-22] @the_wilderless 💜 13

i signed up for singing lessons cause i wanted to stop sounding like a duck, but with just the first lesson it's already given me more than i thought
↓
1531091202992443394 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 1
(obligatory disclaimer that i have no idea what i'm talking about and might be misremembering what my teacher said)
↓
1531091204141637632 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 1
first thing is the idea that giving space to the breath and singing through the notes is primary, rather than manipulating tone
↓
1531091205232238594 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 1
another is that it's by _relaxing control_ do we get space, which actually increases range and 'actual' control

https://t.co/iMnXZ5W5LY
  [Quoting Tweet 1524817611258830849 (missing)]
↓
1531091206893101058 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 1
what i mean by this is that we usually think we sing through contorting our throat muscles in various ways

turns out that's not the main thing and actually tightens us up
↓
1531091208084373505 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 2
rather, we want to ground ourselves in diaphragmatic breath, which is naturally, always there! 

(something something Awareness)
↓
1531091209279660033 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 2 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
another is that singing should feel good! if it doesn't, we're doing something wrong
↓
1531091210382761984 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 2
the idea that we all have this natural instrument, and that everyone's instrument is different - this is also super neat because even though it's all "voice" - we all have it constructed slightly differently, and working with it feels different to everyone
↓
1531091211678797824 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 3
some reflections on the actual experience of singing:
it's really fun! 

embodied vibrations are nice to experience, and at some point i felt like laughing which was really interesting - maybe singing is helping me loosen up in various parts?
↓
1531091212912013313 [2022-05-30] @vincent_yc_li 💜 2
there's also this thing of just hollering out the note and being OK with my voice cracking in the passaggio (which btw what a poetic term for pointing to that concept) 

trusting in the process, leaning into discomfort, relaxing into screwing up

title: The singing tip that turned into a whole philosophy
summary:
The line that set everything off was @relic_radiation’s: “sing from the part of you that wants to be heard.” It hit so hard @the_wilderless could only reply “Fuck,” then immediately tried to smuggle it into his unhinged embodiment drill “The Mead Hall” (jumping/swaying/shouting until it takes you over). The core claim underneath the quote: stop chasing a “better voice” and start expressing the thing in you that actually wants contact.

You can watch the idea evolve from vibes to doctrine. Early on it’s just yearning (“I need to learn to sing… sorry, to wail” from @natural_hazard) and low-stakes social proof (@goblinodds telling @dschorno to put “beautiful singing voice” on a dating profile). Then it gets somatic: @vincent_yc_li reports his teacher’s surprisingly strict heuristic—“singing should feel good! if it doesn’t, we’re doing something wrong”—plus breath/relaxation over throat contortions. After the viral quote, @AskYatharth generalizes it into a creative rule (“write from the part of you that wants to say something… the rest is a distraction”) and later goes full mystic-technique: movement initiates breath, “the body already knows how to sing,” singing as “intimacy with the voice and breath,” and pleasure as the metric.

The peak is when the quote becomes a reusable mental move that people slap onto everything: @danallison reframes stage presence as “Presence from the part of you that wants to be presenced” in response to @goblinodds asking how to learn stage presence, and @AskYatharth piles on (“it’s simple and points to the thing we can start doing now”). After that, the thread kind of stops arguing and starts *shipping*: @bashu_thanks runs a collaborative rap track (“Get Shit Done”) as a proof-of-work counter to “talking about creating,” and later you see the quieter personal practice notes—tuning while singing by feel (@univrsw3th4rt) and the distilled end state: @tasshinfogleman’s “i feel better when i sing.” Why care: it’s a neat internet case study of one sticky sentence turning technical self-improvement into an embodiment/creative permission structure—and it’s genuinely useful if perfectionism is what’s keeping you silent.
